items.title: 68091_Joe Turner oral history interview
items.q: They was the favorite blues singers... T-Bone Walker.

ctx.x: I don't know. I done got kinda lazy on me or forgetful or somethin' here lately. I could sit down now and make up a song. I made up a coupla songs 'bout three...four weeks ago for Norman Granz. Me and Eddie Vinson "Cleanhead" was out there doin' a session with Count Basie so we done a coupla numbers. Then we done a coupla numbers of T-Bone Walker's numbers. And I wrote a couple right there on the spot.
Right there in the studio, huh?

items.title: 68091_Joe Turner oral history interview
items.q: So, the meantime, we was goin' to another club where T-Bone worked at, an' I met my first wife there.

ctx.x: He played the saxophone. He look like he about four feet...he's about the size of Mickey Rooney. Little, bitty short dude.

So, I came to Chicago. Had one place I hadn't played. I'd been skippin' all aroun' Chicago. So we went...I started workin' in a place that Ethel Waters owned...in a nightclub. Pete Johnson and myself, we got a job at Ethel Waters's nightclub. So, the meantime, we was goin' to another club where T-Bone worked at, an' I met my first wife there. She was a flower girl...sold cigarettes and candy an' flowers an' dolls an' stuff. So I met her in the nightclub. So she lived at the Woodside Hotel. So, we were livin'--me…
